events.title: AR-060 — typed registry and reproducible public execution integration
events.description: Begin AR-060 incrementally in the existing cross-rail lab with typed public product metadata, expandable registry-driven navigation, bounded deterministic execution evidence and explicit AI fallback. Preserve private engines and existing URLs. Full SaaS integration, official standards validation and public API deployment remain incomplete.

events.title: AR-061 — shared React payment workbench with executed flow evidence
events.description: Add an incremental React/TypeScript/Vite/Tailwind/Lucide workbench using the public registry and existing deterministic engine, side-by-side synthetic JSON editors, review-and-revalidate correction, execution-derived React Flow nodes and arrows, explicit AI fallback, BLOCKED unsupported conversion, downloads and IndexedDB draft recovery. Existing pages remain accessible. Full message conversion, anonymous APIs, private adapters and official validation remain pending.

events.title: AR-062 — public no-login AML and channel learning tool integration
events.description: Extend the existing React workbench rather than replace it. Add cross-rail AddressTune panel, deterministic fictional-name watchlist screening with temporary in-browser entries, and labelled REST/MQ/Kafka/File/SFTP synthetic handoff demonstrations. Add unit and Playwright checks and rebuild the workbench from source in CI and the Pages release workflow. No live sanctions providers, actual brokers, Gemini API, real bank networks or complete message formats are implemented by this change.

events.title: AR-063 — Payment Rail workbench as primary entry point with homepage-matched branding
events.description: Restyle the existing React payment workbench to the established AddressRail homepage palette of warm ivory, charcoal navigation, soft-blue actions and copper accents without replacing functional tests or banking logic. Reframe the public repository README as a Payment Rail and Transaction Simulation Learning Platform, make /studio/workbench/ the primary launch URL and preserve existing educational pages. No real networks, bank settlement, live Gemini or official scheme certification.

events.title: Publish refreshed homepage-matched workbench assets
events.description: Rebuild and commit the current AR-062/AR-063 workbench assets from the latest source so static previews and GitHub Pages both receive the warm ivory, charcoal and soft-blue theme. Set the initial page canvas and browser theme to warm ivory and preserve the newer screening and channel tools.

events.title: Protected opt-in Gemini review for CBPR+ and SEPA workbench
events.description: Connect the existing Render Gemini service to synthetic CBPR+, SCT, SCT Inst, SDD Core and SDD B2B workbench checks. Preserve synthetic consent, Turnstile and quotas; forward only bounded rail/stage/finding-code evidence. Display provider/model provenance separately from deterministic fallback, no retrieval citations when retrieval is absent, and human review. Browser provider tests use mocks; live deployment and genuine provider verification must be checked separately.

events.title: Grounded workbench AI with bounded LangGraph review
events.description: Extend the protected Gemini workbench with rail-scoped curated lexical retrieval, linked source provenance, a bounded LangGraph workflow and two typed read-only tools, versioned prompts and constrained output, independent citation/finding/safety checks, offline and opt-in live evaluation harnesses, and local human-review acknowledgement. No autonomous payment actions, official validation, semantic-accuracy guarantee or production fairness claim. Deployment and genuine provider success require separate verification.

events.title: Extend opt-in Gemini to all 43 public educational payment contexts
events.description: Allow every registered synthetic payment context to request the protected existing Gemini explanation after executing limited deterministic checks and passing consent/Turnstile. Add 38 public-safe authored-context retrieval summaries alongside existing five scheme-specific examples, and keep backend rail validation and client registry aligned with tests. Generic descriptions are educational context, not authoritative MT/MX rules or payment scheme certification. Private R1/R2/R3 research archives remain exclusively in addressrail-network-core; no private text, actual bank data, or free-tier transfer of proprietary sources is authorised. Live Google calls and Render/GitHub Pages deployment require separate verification.

events.title: Explicit ISO base-XSD version registration groundwork
events.description: Introduce a fail-closed, provenance-pinned public catalogue that registers exactly installed ISO base-XSD message versions and explicitly rejects unsupported pain, pacs and camt variants. Include isolated CI regression tests. This does not add new XSDs, MT parsing or authoritative Swift/rail scheme policy checks; private rules and proprietary sources remain in the private repository.

events.title: Exact source-version retrieval filter for RAG
events.description: Add optional exact-match source-version filtering to investigation TF-IDF retrieval, while preserving effective-date checks and fail-closed invalid filter handling. Test SR2025 and SR2026 metadata isolation with synthetic records. No embedding model, licensed rulebook ingestion, live Gemini certification or payment authority.

events.title: MT/MX first-screen message validator with review-only correction and bounded Gemini/RAG explanations
events.description: Public Workbench starts with SWIFT MT and ISO MX selection. Users may paste synthetic FIN or ISO pain/pacs/camt text, inspect bounded browser-only syntax findings, explicitly approve safe evidence-preserving text corrections, and optionally obtain RAG/Gemini explanations via the existing protected API using finding codes only. This is not arbitrary-message repair, installed XSD execution, comprehensive FIN field validation or certified scheme conformance.

events.title: FX trade XML recognition and RAG route fix
events.description: Recognise four-letter ISO business area identifiers, add targeted archived FX instruction structure checks, and route MT/MX explanations to the protected RAG workflow. These educational checks do not provide exact-version schema validation.

events.title: Inline MT/MX validator placed atop existing payment Workbench navigation
events.description: Move the MT/MX message review into the original Workbench shell with persistent SWIFT/SEPA/UK product navigation. Place a prominent MT/MX validator link above the Products list in the left sidebar and render the two format choices and message editor inside the existing workspace. Preserve the previous product-specific testing, tools, and synthetic correction/Gemini safeguards. No new XSD, FIN, scheme or real-payment validation is claimed.

events.title: Customer-facing error-first MT/MX Workbench
events.description: Keep MT/MX validator within existing top sidebar navigation and two format cards, simplify page content to error, exact field location, reason and suggested correction, remove lengthy technical banners/corpus status and default fallback metadata. AI recommendation button uses vendor-neutral copy while preserving explicit external AI consent, Turnstile, provenance validation and no raw message forwarding. Explicit human approval remains required for deterministic text corrections. Parser and scheme support are unchanged except displaying actual BIC element locations. This does not claim full SWIFT FIN, ISO XSD or scheme certification.

events.title: Field-level message validation and actionable AI findings
events.description: Add targeted missing required FIN MT103/MT202 field checks, limited amount/date/fee checks, and exact-version XML shape checks for pacs.008.001.13/14, pain.001.001.09 and camt.053.001.14 alongside the earlier fxtr.014.001.05 subset. Unsupported versions fail closed instead of appearing validated. Add a deliberately faulty sample for immediate error review and suppress generic AI prompts when no findings. Transfer only bounded error codes and field paths to protected RAG; provider fallback now recommends specific, non-invented actions by location. These are not complete FIN, official XSD or scheme-specific validators.

events.title: Concise success screen with message facts and no generic AI narrative
events.description: For MT/MX local format checks that return no findings, display a concise checks-passed state and message fields extracted only from the supplied content (type, reference, available amount, currency and date). Do not ask a model or display generic advice, recommendation lists or policy narration on clean local checks. Existing targeted errors keep their path, reason and fix guidance. No claim of full official FIN/XSD, scheme validity, settlement or payment authorisation is implied by passing the installed subset checks.

events.title: MT/MX translation preview and postal address structuring tool in one Workbench
events.description: Add a Convert to MX/MT action before load-sample buttons in the existing Workbench. Support bounded MT103↔pacs.008.001.13/.14 and MT202↔pacs.009.001.11/.12 draft field mappings, with mandatory explicit gaps and source restoration. Missing input on Convert uses a documented sample; unsupported pairs fail closed. Add a third Postal Address Converter choice between MT and MX with input and ISO 20022 PstlAdr XML output. From free text or supported MT/MX postal elements, map only explicit/recognised town, country, street, building and postcode, highlight incomplete hybrid or structured previews, escape input and never fabricate payment or routing details. Swift Registered Payment Applications are self-attested postal address tools, not general MT/MX conversion certificates; no product-specific implementation copied or official scheme/XSD conformance implied.
